title: Does a pole in the self-energy imply a violation of the Luttinger theorem?
abstract: Luttinger theorem relates Fermi surface volume to electron density per spin $n$. It holds in an arbitrary Fermi liquid but is widely believed to break when a fermionic self-energy has a pole.   We show that this is not necessarily the case.   As an example, we consider a fermionic system consisting of two gapped bands, originating from a self-energy $Σ(ω, \mathbf{k})$ with a pole,   and a narrow residual quasiparticle band crossing $ω=0$, with a small residue $Z \ll 1$   (a residual Fermi liquid). We consider Model I, in which $Z$ also renormalizes quasiparticle bandwidth $W$ to $ZW$ and Model II, in which $W$ remains unrenormalized.   The Green's function for such a system $G(ω, \mathbf{k})$ contains two zeros and three poles --- one from the quasiparticle band and two from the gapped bands.   Yet, we show that in Model I, the Luttinger-Ward analysis is fully applicable   for any $Z >0$,   and the results are exactly the same as if the gapped bands did not exist. For Model II, the Luttinger-Ward analysis recovers once $Z$ exceeds some critical value, which depends on fermionic density.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates whether a pole in the fermionic self-energy forces a breakdown of the Luttinger theorem. By analyzing two specific models, the authors demonstrate that the Luttinger theorem remains intact, showing that the standard relations hold even when the self-energy exhibits poles, provided the system retains a residual Fermi liquid character.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the presence of a pole in the fermionic self-energy necessarily implies a violation of the Luttinger theorem, which links Fermi surface volume to electron density.
main_result: The Luttinger-Ward analysis shows that the theorem remains valid ($I_1 = n, I_2 = 0$) in both considered models, even when the self-energy has poles, provided a residual Fermi liquid component exists.
method: The authors use the Luttinger-Ward analysis, calculating integrals $I_1$ and $I_2$ derived from the full Green's function, and compare results for two distinct model setups (Model I and Model II).
model_or_system: The system is a fermionic model comprising two gapped bands (whose self-energy has a pole) coupled to a narrow residual quasiparticle band forming a residual Fermi liquid. Two specific models (Model I and Model II) are analyzed based on how the residue $Z$ renormalizes the bandwidth.
key_observables: Luttinger-Ward integrals ($I_1$ and $I_2$), the chemical potential ($\mu_\Delta$), and the Density of States $N(\omega)$.
important_parameters: The residue $Z$ of the pole, the bandwidth $W$, and the fermionic density $n$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the Luttinger-Ward analysis and compares results across the limit $Z 	o 0^+$ to study continuity/discontinuity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Density of States $N(\omega)$ for Model I and Model II, and plot the chemical potential $\mu_\Delta$ and the integral $I_2$ as functions of system parameters like $\Delta/W$ and $Z$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes two models (Model I and Model II) by calculating the Luttinger-Ward integrals $I_1$ and $I_2$ using the full Green's function. It compares the results for $Z>0$ versus $Z=0$, demonstrating the persistence of the Luttinger theorem in the presence of self-energy poles.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to strongly correlated electron physics as it addresses fundamental theorems (Luttinger's) in regimes where quasiparticle descriptions are challenged by complex self-energies, which is a core topic in modern condensed matter theory.
